text:
maria: quick question — saved views that include a pinned model are behaving oddly when you open them from another route. it drops the pin and falls back to the route default. users are confused. can we make pinned-models portable or at least surface why it changed?
joel: do you have a concrete example? is this for route-to-route copy, or when a saved view is in a workspace shared across routes?
maria: e.g. Alice saves a view on /routes/payment that pins `redwood/fast-1.2`. She shares the view link with Bob who opens it on /routes/checkout. Bob expects the same pinned model but the console shows fallback `redwood/fast-1.0` and a note "model not available for this route" (super terse).
ash (ops-bot): deployment note: model variants can be region- and capacity-gated (dedicated vs hosted). this can legitimately make a pin unavailable.
ash (ash): to be explicit — the saved-view object currently only stores filters + view layout. We intentionally left routing hints out to avoid leaking customer-specific routing. but maybe we need a small optional metadata chunk `routing_hint` that is safe to store/share.
joel: sketch of what I'm imagining (proposal):
```json
{
  "name": "Errors > high-latency",
  "filters": {"status": "5xx"},
  "pinned_model": "redwood/fast-1.2",
  "routing_hint": {"model_variant": "fast-1.2", "preferred_region": "us-west-2", "quota_tier": "dedicated"}
}
```
elaine: +1 on hints but with caveats: saved views are shared across orgs/teams that may not have access to `dedicated` quota or that region. we should treat `routing_hint` as advisory only and show an explicit fallback UI step. do not let the server try to silently route users into a tier they don't own.
sam: UX suggestion — show a small pill when a view was saved with a model that isn't available: "Saved with: fast-1.2 (not available here)". clicking pill expands: "Open with fallback: fast-1.0" and an action "Request access / Ask admin". keeps the users' mental model intact. :bulb:
maria: telemetry ask — can we track when a pinned_model is used vs when a fallback was applied? want to know how often views degrade across routes.
ash (ash): yes — add two events: `saved_view.apply_attempt` with metadata {view_id, pinned_model, route_id, used_fallback:true|false, fallback_model}. also emit `saved_view.share_open` when someone opens a view saved on a different route.
joel: question about API compatibility — adding routing_hint should be optional so older clients still work, right?
ash (ash): yup optional. server logic: if `routing_hint` present, we attempt to honor it but only if policies allow. otherwise we do deterministic fallback and return `applied_model` in the response. clients should render both `requested_model` + `applied_model` fields.
elaine: also think we need an ACL consideration — saved views that include `pinned_model` should indicate whether the view is "portable" (i.e., contains only advisory hints) or "locked" (explicitly requires exact model and access). locked views should display a clear access error if opened without entitlement.
maria: ok i'll file a ticket with the API sketch, telemetry events, and a couple mockups for the pill + fallback modal. can someone (cc @joel @ash) add the small JSON snippet to the API spec and note backwards compatibility?
joel: will add spec diff today.
ash (ash): will add telemetry and server side behavior notes.
sam: i'll produce the mock with the pill + request access flow tomorrow.
maria: thanks all. follow up: let's track an experiment flag to roll this out to 10% first, so we can watch how many fallbacks happen and whether it increases support tickets. :rocket:
